<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Company&#146;s Certificate of Incorporation authorizing the changing of the name of the Company from &#147;meVC Draper Fisher Jurvetson Fund I,&nbsp;Inc.&#148; to &#147;MVC Capital,&nbsp;Inc.&#148;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;7, 2004, the Company&#146;s name change from &#147;meVC Draper Fisher Jurvetson Fund I,&nbsp;Inc.&#148; to &#147;MVC Capital,&nbsp;Inc.&#148; became effective.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;16, 2004, the Company commenced the operations of MVC Financial Services,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;MVCFS&#148;).&#160; MVCFS is incorporated in Delaware and its principal purpose is to provide advisory, administrative and other services to the Company and the Company&#146;s Portfolio Companies.&#160; The Company does not hold MVCFS for investment purposes and does not intend to sell MVCFS.&#160; </font>On October&nbsp;14, 2011, the Company formed a wholly-owned subsidiary, MVC Cayman, an exempted company incorporated in the Cayman Islands, to hold certain of its investments.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On September&nbsp;7, 2006, the stockholders of MVC Capital approved the adoption of the investment advisory and management agreement (the &#147;Advisory Agreement&#148;).&#160; The Advisory Agreement, which was entered into on October&nbsp;31, 2006, provides for external management of the Company by TTG Advisers, which is led by Michael Tokarz.&#160; The agreement took effect on November&nbsp;1, 2006.&#160; Upon the effectiveness of the Advisory Agreement, Mr.&nbsp;Tokarz&#146;s employment agreement with the Company terminated.&#160; All of the individuals (including the Company&#146;s investment professionals) that had been previously employed by the Company as of the fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2006 became employees of TTG Advisers.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;11, 2008, our Board of Directors, including all of the directors who are not &#147;interested persons,&#148; as defined under the 1940 Act, of the Company (the &#147;Independent Directors&#148;), at an in-person meeting approved an amended and restated investment advisory and management agreement (also, the &#147;Advisory Agreement&#148;), which was approved by stockholders of the Company on April&nbsp;14, 2009. The renewal of the Advisory Agreement was last approved by the Independent Directors at their in-person meeting held on October&nbsp;31, 2019.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">2.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b>Consolidation</b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;16, 2004, the Company formed a wholly-owned subsidiary, MVC Financial Services,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;MVCFS&#148;).&#160; MVCFS is incorporated in Delaware and its principal purpose is to provide advisory, administrative and other services to the Company, the Company&#146;s portfolio companies and other entities.&#160; MVCFS had opening equity of $1 (100 shares at $0.01 per share). The Company does not hold MVCFS for investment purposes and does not intend to sell MVCFS.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;14, 2011, the Company formed a wholly-owned subsidiary, MVC Cayman, an exempted company incorporated in the Cayman Islands, to hold certain of its investments and to make certain future investments.&#160; The results of MVCFS and MVC Cayman are consolidated into the Company and all inter-company accounts have been eliminated in consolidation.&#160; Of the $11.7 million in cash and cash equivalents on the Company&#146;s Consolidated Balance Sheets as of October&nbsp;31, 2019, approximately $1.1 million was held by MVC Cayman.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2012 and thereafter, MVC Partners, LLC (&#147;MVC Partners&#148;) was consolidated with the operations of the Company as MVC Partners&#146; limited partnership interest in the MVC Private Equity Fund, L.P. (&#147;PE Fund&#148;) is a substantial portion of MVC Partners operations.&#160; Previously, MVC Partners was presented as a portfolio company on the Consolidated Schedule of Investments.&#160; The consolidation of MVC Partners has not had any</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">material effect on the financial position or net results of operations of the Company.&#160; There are additional disclosures resulting from this consolidation.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">MVC GP II, LLC (&#147;MVC GP II&#148;), an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, serves as the general partner to the PE Fund.&nbsp; MVC GP II is wholly-owned by MVCFS, a subsidiary of the Company.&nbsp; The results of MVC GP II are consolidated into MVCFS and ultimately the Company.&nbsp;All inter-company accounts have been eliminated in consolidation.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:23.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2014, MVC Turf,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;MVC Turf&#148;) was consolidated with the Company as MVC Turf is an MVC wholly-owned holding company. The consolidation of MVC Turf did not have any material effect on the financial position or net results of operations of the Company.&#160; On March&nbsp;7, 2017, the Company exchanged its shares of MVC Turf, the holding company that owned the Company&#146;s LLC interest in Turf Products, for approximately $3.8 million of additional subordinated debt in Turf Products.&nbsp; Prior to the exchange, the Company also received a distribution from MVC Turf of approximately $323,000. The impact of the deconsolidation of MVC Turf on the Company&#146;s financial condition and results of operations was immaterial.&#160; As of October&nbsp;31, 2017, MVC Turf is no longer consolidated with the Company.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">3.</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b>Significant Accounting Policies</b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following is a summary of significant accounting policies followed by the Company in the preparation of its consolidated financial statements:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The preparation of consolidated financial statements in conformity with U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (&#147;GAAP&#148;) requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts and disclosures in the consolidated financial statements.&#160; Actual results could differ from those estimates.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:23.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</font></i> &#151; In May&nbsp;2014, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#147;FASB&#148;) issued Accounting Standards Update (&#147;ASU&#148;) No.&nbsp;2014-09, &#147;Revenue from Contracts with Customers&#148; (Topic 606). ASU 2014-09 addresses the reporting of revenue by most entities and will replace most existing revenue recognition guidance in U.S. GAAP when it becomes effective. In August&nbsp;2015, the FASB issued ASU 2015-14 that defers the effective date of ASU 2014-09 for public business entities for annual reporting periods beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2017, including interim periods therein. Early application is not permitted for public business entities.&#160; On December&nbsp;27, 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-20&nbsp;to make various amendments to Topic 606, going into effect for years beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2017.&#160; The standard impacted the fair value of the PE Fund&#146;s LP interest due to the exclusion of the Company&#146;s portion of the carried interest associated with the PE Fund.&#160; This update has had no material impact on our financial statements.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:23.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August&nbsp;2014, FASB issued ASU 2014-15, &#147;Presentation of Financial Statements &#151; Going Concern (Subtopic 205-40): Disclosure of Uncertainties about an Entity&#146;s Ability to Continue as a Going Concern&#148; (&#147;ASU 2014-15&#148;). The standard requires management to evaluate, at each interim and annual reporting period, whether there are conditions or events that raise substantial doubt about the entity&#146;s ability to continue as a going concern within one year after the date the financial statements are issued, and provide related disclosures. ASU 2014-15 is effective for annual periods ending after December&nbsp;15, 2016, and for annual and interim periods thereafter, and early adoption is permitted. This update has had no impact on our financial statements.</font></p>

Additionally, a</font>  </font>private company electing the alternative is required to provide detailed disclosures about its involvement with, and exposure to, the legal entity under common control.&#160; The ASU also amends the guidance for determining whether a decision-making fee is a variable interest.&#160; The amendments require organizations to consider indirect interests held through related parties under common control on a proportional basis rather than as the equivalent of a direct interest in its entirety (as currently required in GAAP). The ASU is effective for public business entities for fiscal years and interim periods beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2019. The Company does not expect the adoption of ASU 2018-17 to have a material impact on our financial statements.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Valuation of Investments </font></i>&#151; The Accounting Standards Codification (&#147;ASC&#148;),<i> Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures </i>(&#147;ASC 820&#148;), defines fair value in terms of the price that would be received upon the sale of an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. The price used to measure the fair value is not adjusted for transaction costs while the cost basis of our investments may include initial transaction costs. Under ASC 820, the fair value measurement also assumes that the transaction to sell an asset occurs in the principal market for the asset or, in the absence of a principal market, the most advantageous market for the asset. The principal market is the market in which the reporting entity would sell or transfer the asset with the greatest volume and level of activity for the asset to which the reporting entity has access as of the measurement date.&#160; If no market for the asset exists or if the reporting entity does not have access to the principal market, the reporting entity should use a hypothetical market.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pursuant to the requirements of the 1940 Act and in accordance with ASC 820, we value our portfolio securities at their current market values or, if market quotations are not readily available, at their estimates of fair values. Because our portfolio company investments generally do not have readily ascertainable market values, we record these investments at fair value in accordance with our Valuation Procedures adopted by the Board of Directors, which are consistent with ASC 820.&#160; As permitted by the SEC, the Board of Directors has delegated the responsibility of making fair value determinations to the Valuation Committee, subject to the Board of Directors&#146; supervision and pursuant to our Valuation Procedures.&#160; Our Board of Directors may also hire independent consultants to review our Valuation Procedures or to conduct an independent valuation of one or more of our portfolio investments.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pursuant to our Valuation Procedures, the Valuation Committee (which is comprised of three Independent Directors) determines fair values of portfolio company investments on a quarterly basis (or more frequently, if deemed appropriate under the circumstances). In doing so, the Committee considers the recommendations of The Tokarz Group Advisers LLC (&#147;TTG Advisers&#148;).&#160; The Committee also takes into account input and reviews by third party consultants retained to support the Company&#146;s valuation process. The Company has also adopted several other enhanced processes related to valuations of controlled/affiliated portfolio companies.&#160; Any changes in valuation are recorded in the consolidated statements of operations as &#147;Net unrealized appreciation (depreciation) on investments.&#148;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Currently, our NAV per share is calculated and published on a quarterly basis.&#160; The Company calculates our NAV per share by subtracting all liabilities from the total value of our portfolio securities and other assets and dividing the result by the total number of outstanding shares of our common stock on the date of valuation.&#160; Fair values of foreign investments reflect exchange rates,</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">as applicable, in effect on the last business day of the quarter end.&#160; Exchange rates fluctuate on a daily basis, sometimes significantly.&#160; Exchange rate fluctuations following the most recent fiscal year end</font>  </font>are not reflected in the valuations reported in this Annual Report.&#160; See Item 1A Risk Factor, &#147;Investments in foreign debt or equity may involve significant risks in addition to the risks inherent in U.S. investments.&#148;</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:18.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At October&nbsp;31, 2019 and October&nbsp;31, 2018, approximately 92.6% and 86.5%, respectively, of total assets represented investments in portfolio companies recorded at fair value (&#147;Fair Value Investments&#148;).</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under most circumstances, at the time of acquisition, Fair Value Investments are carried at cost (absent the existence of conditions warranting, in management&#146;s and the Valuation Committee&#146;s view, a different initial value).&#160; During the period that an investment is held by the Company, its original cost may cease to approximate fair value as the result of market and investment specific factors.&#160; No pre-determined formula can be applied to determine fair value.&#160; Rather, the Valuation Committee analyzes fair value measurements based on the value at which the securities of the portfolio company could be sold in an orderly disposition over a reasonable period of time between willing parties, other than in a forced or liquidation sale.&#160; The liquidity event whereby the Company ultimately exits an investment is generally the sale, the merger, the recapitalization of a portfolio company or by a public offering of its securities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There is no one methodology to determine fair value and, in fact, for any portfolio security, fair value may be expressed as a range of values, from which the Company derives a single estimate of fair value.&#160; To determine the fair value of a portfolio security, the Valuation Committee analyzes the portfolio company&#146;s financial results and projections, publicly traded comparable companies when available, comparable private transactions when available, precedent transactions in the market when available, third-party real estate and asset appraisals if appropriate and available, discounted cash flow analysis, if appropriate, as well as other factors.&#160; The Company generally requires, where practicable, portfolio companies to provide annual audited and more regular unaudited financial statements, and/or annual projections for the upcoming fiscal year.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The fair value of our portfolio securities is inherently subjective. Because of the inherent uncertainty of fair valuation of portfolio securities and escrow receivables that do not have readily ascertainable market values, our estimate of fair value may significantly differ from the fair value that would have been used had a ready market existed for the securities. Such values also do not reflect brokers&#146; fees or other selling costs, which might become payable on disposition of such investments.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">If a security is publicly traded, the fair value is generally equal to market value based on the closing price on the principal exchange on which the security is primarily traded unless restricted and a restricted discount is applied.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For equity securities of portfolio companies, whose securities are not publicly traded, the Valuation Committee estimates the fair value based on market and/or income approach with value then attributed to equity or equity like securities using the enterprise value waterfall (&#147;Enterprise Value Waterfall&#148;) valuation methodology.&#160; Under the Enterprise Value Waterfall valuation methodology, the Valuation Committee estimates the enterprise fair value of the portfolio company and then waterfalls the enterprise value over the portfolio company&#146;s securities in order of their preference relative to one another.&#160; To assess the enterprise value of the portfolio company, the</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;">114<a name="PB_114_121623_7748"></a></p>

<div style="page-break-before:always;"></div>
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">Valuation Committee weighs some or all of the traditional market valuation methods and factors</font>  </font>based on the individual circumstances of the portfolio company in order to estimate the enterprise value.&#160; The methodologies for performing assets may be based on, among other things:&#160; valuations of comparable public companies, recent sales of private and public comparable companies, discounting the forecasted cash flows of the portfolio company, third party valuations of the portfolio company, considering offers from third parties to buy the company, estimating the value to potential strategic buyers and considering the value of recent investments in the equity securities of the portfolio company, and third-party asset and real estate appraisals.&#160; For non-performing assets, the Valuation Committee may estimate the liquidation or collateral value of the portfolio company&#146;s assets.&#160; The Valuation Committee also takes into account historical and anticipated financial results.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company does not utilize hedge accounting and instead, when applicable, marks its derivatives to market on the Company&#146;s consolidated statement of operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In assessing enterprise value, the Valuation Committee considers the mergers and acquisitions (&#147;M&amp;A&#148;) market as the principal market in which the Company would sell its investments in portfolio companies under circumstances where the Company has the ability to control or gain control of the board of directors of the portfolio company (&#147;Control Companies&#148;).&#160; This approach is consistent with the principal market that the Company would use for its portfolio companies if the Company has the ability to initiate a sale of the portfolio company as of the measurement date, i.e., if it has the ability to control or gain control of the board of directors of the portfolio company as of the measurement date.&#160; In evaluating if the Company can control or gain control of a portfolio company as of the measurement date, the Company takes into account its equity securities on a fully diluted basis, as well as other factors.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For Non-Control Companies, consistent with ASC 820, the Valuation Committee considers a hypothetical secondary market as the principal market in which it would sell investments in those companies.&#160; The Company also considers other valuation methodologies such as the Option Pricing Method and liquidity preferences when valuing minority equity positions of a portfolio company.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For loans and debt securities of Non-Control Companies (for which the Valuation Committee has identified the hypothetical secondary market as the principal market), the Valuation Committee determines fair value based on the assumptions that a hypothetical market participant would use to value the security in a current hypothetical sale using a market yield (&#147;Market Yield&#148;) valuation methodology.&#160; In applying the Market Yield valuation methodology, the Valuation Committee determines the fair value based on such factors as third party broker quotes (if available) and market participant assumptions, including synthetic credit ratings, estimated remaining life, current market yield and interest rate spreads of similar securities as of the measurement date.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Estimates of average life are generally based on market data of the average life of similar debt securities.&#160; However, if the Valuation Committee has information available to it that the debt security is expected to be repaid in the near term, the Valuation Committee would use an estimated life based on the expected repayment date.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Valuation Committee determines fair value of loan and debt securities of Control Companies based on the estimate of the enterprise value of the portfolio company.&#160; To the extent the enterprise value exceeds the remaining principal amount of the loan and all other debt securities of the company, the fair value of such securities is generally estimated to be their cost.&#160; However,</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;">115<a name="PB_115_121737_141"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">where the enterprise</font>  </font>value is less than the remaining principal amount of the loan and all other debt securities, the Valuation Committee may discount the value of such securities to reflect an impairment.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the Company&#146;s or its subsidiary&#146;s investment in the PE Fund, for which an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company serves as the general partner (the &#147;GP&#148;) of the PE Fund, the Valuation Committee relies on the GP&#146;s determination of the fair value of the PE Fund which will be generally valued, as a practical expedient, utilizing the net asset valuations provided by the GP, which will be made:&#160; (i)&nbsp;no less frequently than quarterly as of the Company&#146;s fiscal quarter end and (ii)&nbsp;with respect to the valuation of PE Fund investments in portfolio companies, will be based on methodologies consistent with those set forth in the Company&#146;s Valuation Procedures.&#160; In making its determinations, the GP considers and generally relies on TTG Advisers&#146; recommendations.&#160; The determination of the net asset value of the Company&#146;s or its subsidiary&#146;s investment in the PE Fund will follow the methodologies described for valuing interests in private investment funds (&#147;Investment Vehicles&#148;) described below.&#160; Additionally, when both the Company and the PE Fund hold investments in the same portfolio company, the GP&#146;s Fair Value determination shall be based on the Valuation Committee&#146;s determination of the Fair Value of the Company&#146;s portfolio security in that portfolio company.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As permitted under GAAP, the Company&#146;s interests in private investment funds are generally valued, as a practical expedient, utilizing the net asset valuations provided by management of the underlying Investment Vehicles, without adjustment, unless TTG Advisers is aware of information indicating that a value reported does not accurately reflect the value of the Investment Vehicle, including any information showing that the valuation has not been calculated in a manner consistent with GAAP.&#160; Net unrealized appreciation (depreciation) of such investments is recorded based on the Company&#146;s proportionate share of the aggregate amount of appreciation (depreciation) recorded by each underlying Investment Vehicle.&#160; The Company&#146;s proportionate investment interest includes its share of interest and dividend income and expense, and realized and unrealized gains and losses on securities held by the underlying Investment Vehicles, net of operating expenses and fees.&#160; Realized gains and losses on distributions from Investment Vehicles are generally recognized on a first in, first out basis.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company applies the practical expedient to interests in Investment Vehicles on an investment by investment basis, and consistently with respect to the Company&#146;s entire interest in an investment.&#160; The Company may adjust the valuation obtained from an Investment Vehicle with a premium, discount or reserve if it determines that the net asset value is not representative of fair value.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">If the Company intends to sell all or a portion of its interest in an Investment Vehicle to a third-party in a privately negotiated transaction near the valuation date, the Company will consider offers from third parties to buy the interest in an Investment Vehicle in valuations which may be discounted for both probability of close and time.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">When the Company receives nominal cost warrants or free equity securities (&#147;nominal cost equity&#148;) with a debt security, the Company typically allocates its cost basis in the investment between debt securities and nominal cost equity at the time of origination.&#160; If the Company is not reimbursed for investment or transaction related costs at the time an investment is made, the Company typically capitalizes those costs to the cost basis of the investment.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest income, adjusted for amortization of premium and accretion of discount on a yield to maturity methodology, is recorded on an accrual basis to the extent that such amounts are expected to be collected.&#160; Origination and/or closing fees associated with investments in portfolio companies are accreted into income over the respective terms of the applicable loans.&#160; Upon the prepayment of a loan or debt security, any unamortized original issue discount or market discount is recorded as interest income. Prepayment premiums are recorded on loans when received as interest income.&#160; Dividend income, if any, is recognized on an accrual basis on the ex-dividend date to the extent that the Company expects to collect such amounts.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For loans, debt securities, and preferred securities with contractual payment-in-kind interest or dividends, which represent contractual interest/dividends accrued and added to the loan balance or liquidation preference that generally becomes due at maturity, the Company will not ascribe value to payment-in-kind interest/dividends, if the portfolio company valuation indicates that the payment-in-kind interest is not collectible.&#160; However, the Company may ascribe value to payment-in-kind interest if the health of the portfolio company and the underlying securities are not in question.&#160; All payment-in-kind interest that has been added to the principal balance or capitalized is subject to ratification by the Valuation Committee.&#160;&#160; For interest or deferred interest receivables purchased by the Company at a discount to their outstanding amount, the Company amortizes the discount using the effective yield method and records it as interest income over the life of the loan.&#160; The Company will not ascribe value to the interest or deferred interest, if the Company has determined that the interest is not collectible.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Escrows from the sale of a portfolio company are generally valued at an amount, which may be expected to be received from the buyer under the escrow&#146;s various conditions and discounted for both risk and time.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ASC 460, <i>Guarantees</i>, requires the Company to estimate the fair value of the guarantee obligation at its inception and requires the Company to assess whether a probable loss contingency exists in accordance with the requirements of ASC 450, Contingencies.&#160; The Valuation Committee typically will look at the pricing of the security in which the guarantee provided support for the security and compare it to the price of a similar or hypothetical security without guarantee support.&#160; The difference in pricing will be discounted for time and risk over the period in which the guarantee is expected to remain outstanding.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Investment Classification</font></u></i> &#151;As defined in the 1940 Act, &#147;Control Investments&#148; are investments in those companies that we are deemed to &#147;Control.&#148;&#160; &#147;Affiliate Investments&#148; are investments in those companies that are &#147;Affiliated Companies&#148; of us, as defined in the 1940 Act, other than Control Investments.&#160; &#147;Non-Control/Non-Affiliate Investments&#148; are those that are neither Control Investments nor Affiliate Investments.&#160; Generally, under that 1940 Act, we are deemed to control a company in which we have invested if we own 25% or more of the voting securities of such company or have greater than 50% representation on its board.&#160; We are deemed to be an affiliate of a company in which we have invested if we own 5% or more and less than 25% of the voting securities of such company.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Investment Transactions and Related Operating Income</font></u></i> &#151; Investment transactions and related revenues and expenses are accounted for on the trade date.&#160; The cost of securities sold is determined on a first-in, first-out basis, unless otherwise specified.&#160; Dividend income and distributions on investment securities is recorded on the ex-dividend date.&#160; The tax characteristics of such distributions received from our Portfolio Companies will be determined by whether or not the</p>

Interest income, which includes accretion of discount and amortization of premium, if applicable, is recorded on the accrual basis to the extent that such amounts are expected to be collected.&#160; Fee income includes fees for guarantees and services rendered by the Company or its wholly-owned subsidiary to Portfolio Companies and other third parties such as due diligence, structuring, transaction services, monitoring services, and investment advisory services. Guaranty fees are recognized as income over the related period of the guaranty. Due diligence, structuring, and transaction services fees are generally recognized as income when services are rendered or when the related transactions are completed. Upon the prepayment of a loan or debt security, any unamortized original issue discount or market discount is recorded as interest income.&#160; For investments with PIK interest and dividends, we base income and dividend accrual on the valuation of the PIK notes or securities received from the borrower.&#160; If the portfolio company indicates a value of the PIK notes or securities that is not sufficient to cover the contractual interest or dividend, the Company does not accrue interest or dividend income on the notes or securities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The functional currency of the Company is the U.S. Dollar. Assets and liabilities denominated in a currency other than the U.S. Dollar are translated into U.S. Dollars at the closing rates of exchange on the date of determination. Purchases and sales of investments and income and expenses denominated in currencies other than U.S. Dollars are translated at the rates of exchange on the respective dates of the transactions. The resulting gains and losses from such currency translation are included in the Consolidated Statement of Operations. The Company does not isolate the portion of the results of operations resulting from the changes in foreign exchange rates on investments from the fluctuation arising from changes in fair values of securities held. Such fluctuations are included with the Net Realized and Unrealized Gain (Loss) on Investments and foreign currency in the Consolidated Statement of Operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Cash and Cash Equivalents - </font></u></i>For the purpose of the Consolidated Balance Sheets and Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, the Company considers all money market and all highly liquid temporary cash investments purchased with an original maturity of less than three months to be cash equivalents. The Company places its cash and cash equivalents with financial institutions and cash held in bank accounts may exceed the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (&#147;FDIC&#148;) insured limit.&#160; As of October&nbsp;31, 2019, the Company had approximately $5.4 million in cash equivalents, approximately $5.0 million in restricted cash equivalents and approximately $1.3 million in cash totaling approximately $11.7 million.&#160; Of the $1.3 million in cash and the $5.4 million in cash equivalents, approximately $1.0 million and $99,000, respectively, was held by MVC Cayman.&#160; As of October&nbsp;31, 2018, the Company had approximately $783,000 in cash equivalents, approximately $5.3 million in restricted cash and approximately $9.8 million in cash totaling approximately $15.9 million.&#160; Of the $9.8 million in cash and $783,000 in cash equivalents, approximately $1.0 million and $100,000, respectively, was held by MVC Cayman.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">provided by a third party financial institution that MVC collateralized with cash, that was classified as restricted cash on the Company&#146;s Consolidated Balance Sheets and was not a commitment as of October&nbsp;31, 2019.&#160; Also, as of October&nbsp;31, 2018 and October&nbsp;31, 2019, the Company had restricted cash or cash equivalents of $5.0 million related to the compensating balance requirement for Credit Facility III and Credit Facility IV (defined below), respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Restricted Securities</font></u></i> &#151; The Company may invest in privately placed restricted securities.&#160; These securities may be resold in transactions exempt from registration or to the public if the securities are registered.&#160; Disposal of these securities may involve time-consuming negotiations and expense, and a prompt sale at an acceptable price may be difficult.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Reclassifications</font></u></i> &#151; Certain amounts from prior years have been reclassified to conform to the current year presentation.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Distributions to Shareholders</font></u></i> &#151; Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes</font></u></i> &#151; To be taxed as a regulated investment company (&#147;RIC&#148;), the Company is required (amongst other things) to distribute to its shareholders, in a timely manner, at least 90% of its investment company taxable income and 90% of its net tax-exempt income each year.&#160; If the Company distributes, in a calendar year, at least 98% of its ordinary income and 98.2% of its capital gain net income for the one year period ending October&nbsp;31<font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">st</font>&#160;of such calendar year (as well as any undistributed amounts from previous years), it will not be liable for to the 4% non-deductible federal excise tax on certain undistributed income of RICs.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our consolidated operating subsidiary, MVCFS, is subject to federal and state income tax.&#160; We use the liability method in accounting for income taxes.&#160; Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recorded for temporary differences between the tax basis of assets and liabilities and their reported amounts in the financial statements, using statutory tax rates in effect for the year in which the differences are expected to reverse.&#160; A valuation allowance is provided against deferred tax assets when it is more likely than not that some portion or all of the deferred tax asset will not be realized.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ASC 740,&nbsp;<i>Income Taxes</i>, provides guidance for how uncertain tax positions should be recognized, measured, presented and disclosed in the financial statements. ASC 740 requires the evaluation of tax positions taken or expected to be taken in the course of preparing the Company&#146;s tax returns to determine whether the tax positions are &#147;more-likely-than-not&#148; of being sustained by the applicable tax authority. Tax positions deemed to meet a &#147;more-likely-than-not&#148; threshold would be recorded as a tax benefit or expense in the current period. There were no uncertain tax positions as of October&nbsp;31, 2019 that needed to be recorded or disclosed on the financial statements.&#160; The Company recognizes interest and penalties, if any, related to unrecognized tax benefits as income tax expense in the consolidated statement of operations. During the fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2019, the Company did not incur any interest or penalties.&#160; Although we file federal and state tax returns, our major tax jurisdiction is federal for the Company and MVCFS.&#160; The fiscal years 2015, 2016, 2017 and 2018 for the Company and MVCFS remain subject to examination by the federal, state and local tax authorities.</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">4.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b>Management</b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;6, 2003, Michael Tokarz assumed his positions as Chairman, Portfolio Manager and Director of the Company. From November&nbsp;6, 2003 to October&nbsp;31, 2006, the Company was internally managed.&#160; Effective November&nbsp;1, 2006, Mr.&nbsp;Tokarz&#146;s employment agreement with the Company terminated and the obligations under that agreement were superseded by those under the Advisory Agreement entered into with TTG Advisers.&#160; Under the terms of the Advisory Agreement, the Company pays TTG Advisers a base management fee and an incentive fee for its provision of investment advisory and management services.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Board of Directors, including all of the Independent Directors, last approved a renewal of the Advisory Agreement at their in-person meeting held on October&nbsp;31, 2019.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the terms of the Advisory Agreement, TTG Advisers determines, consistent with the Company&#146;s investment strategy, the composition of the Company&#146;s portfolio, the nature and timing of the changes to the Company&#146;s portfolio and the manner of implementing such changes.&#160; TTG Advisers also identifies and negotiates the structure of the Company&#146;s investments (including performing due diligence on prospective Portfolio Companies), closes and monitors the Company&#146;s investments, determines the securities and other assets purchased, retains or sells and oversees the administration, recordkeeping and compliance functions of the Company and/or third parties performing such functions for the Company.&#160; TTG Advisers&#146; services under the Advisory Agreement are not exclusive, and it may furnish similar services to other entities.&#160; Pursuant to the Advisory Agreement, the Company is required to pay TTG Advisers a fee for investment advisory and management services consisting of two components&#151;a base management fee and an incentive fee.&#160; The base management fee is calculated at 2.0% per annum of the Company&#146;s total assets excluding cash, the value of any investment in a Third-Party Vehicle covered by a Separate Agreement (as defined in the Advisory Agreement) and the value of any investment by the Company not made in portfolio companies (&#147;Non-Eligible Assets&#148;) but including assets purchased with borrowed funds that are not Non-Eligible Assets.&#160; The incentive fee consists of two parts: (i)&nbsp;one part is based on our pre-incentive fee net operating income; and (ii)&nbsp;the other part is based on the capital gains realized on our portfolio of securities acquired after November&nbsp;1, 2003.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:20.25pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Advisory Agreement provides for an expense cap pursuant to which TTG Advisers will absorb or reimburse operating expenses of the Company, to the extent necessary to limit the Company&#146;s expense ratio (the consolidated expenses of the Company, including any amounts payable to TTG Advisers under the base management fee, but excluding the amount of any interest and other direct borrowing costs, taxes, incentive compensation and extraordinary expenses taken as a percentage of the Company&#146;s average net assets) to 3.5% in each of the 2009 and 2010 fiscal years.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On various dates, TTG Advisers and the Company entered into annual agreements to extend the expense cap of 3.5% to the 2011, 2012, 2013 and 2014 fiscal years (&#147;Expense Limitation Agreement&#148;).&#160; The Company and the Adviser agreed to continue the expense cap into fiscal year 2015 and fiscal year 2016, though they lowered the expense cap to 3.25% and modified the methodology so that the cap is applied to limit the Company&#146;s ratio of expenses to total assets less cash (the &#147;Modified Methodology&#148;), consistent with the asset level used to calculate the base management fee. (The expenses covered by the cap remain unchanged.)&#160; On October&nbsp;28, 2016, the Board of Directors, including all of the Independent Directors, approved the renewal of the Advisory Agreement for the 2017 fiscal year. Further, the Adviser agreed to continue to waive a</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

(B)&nbsp;If the NAV discount is between 10% and 20%, the management fee will be 1.50%; and (C)&nbsp;If the NAV discount is less than 10% or eliminated, the 1.50% management fee would be re-examined, but in no event would it exceed 1.75%.&#160; <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;29, 2010, through MVC Partners and MVCFS, the Company committed to invest approximately $20.1 million in the PE Fund.&nbsp; The PE Fund has closed on approximately $104 million of capital commitments.&nbsp; The Company&#146;s Board of Directors authorized the establishment of, and investment in, the PE Fund for a variety of reasons, including the Company&#146;s ability to make additional investments that represent more than 5% of its total assets or more than 10% of the outstanding voting securities of the issuer (&#147;Non-Diversified Investments&#148;) through the PE Fund. As previously disclosed, the Company may be restricted in its ability to make Non-Diversified Investments.&nbsp; For services provided to the PE Fund, the GP and MVC Partners are together entitled to receive 25% of all management fees and other fees paid by the PE Fund and its portfolio companies and up to 30% of the carried interest generated by the PE Fund.&#160; Further, at the direction of the Board of Directors, the GP retained TTG Advisers to serve as the portfolio manager of the PE Fund.&#160; In exchange for providing those services, and pursuant to the Board of Directors&#146; authorization and direction, TTG Advisers is entitled to receive the balance of the fees generated by the PE Fund and its portfolio companies and a portion of any carried interest generated by the PE Fund.&#160; Given this separate arrangement with the GP and the PE Fund (the &#147;PM Agreement&#148;), under the terms of the Company&#146;s Advisory Agreement with TTG Advisers, TTG Advisers is not entitled to receive from the Company a management fee or an incentive fee on assets of the Company that are invested in the PE Fund. However, the Company&#146;s limited partnership interest and GP interest in the PE Fund are subject to the PE Fund&#146;s annual management fee, a portion of which, as described above, is retained by the Company and not paid out to TTG Advisers as portfolio</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">5</font>&#160; The NAV discount referred to herein is the average daily discount to NAV for a quarter.&#160; The discount is determined using the most recently determined NAV per share, which is typically the prior quarter end&#146;s NAV per share and the Company stock closing price on any given day for the quarter.</p>

As of October 31, 2018, the balance of the Deferred Portion of the incentive compensation payable was approximately $2.5 million.&#160; During the fiscal year ended October 31, 2019, the Company made an approximately $975,000 incentive compensation payment to TTG Advisers related to the sale of the Crius equity units, resulting in a balance of approximately $1.5 million as of October 31, 2019.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;31, 2019, per the Current Incentive Fee Modification, the Adviser indicated its voluntary agreement to modify the calculation of the Income Incentive Fee for the fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2020, so that the fee accrued </font>shall be subject to the following additional provisions:&#160; (A)&nbsp;in lieu of the &#147;Lower Hurdle Amount&#148; and the &#147;Higher Hurdle Amount&#148; set forth in the Advisory Agreement and in lieu of the Income Incentive Fee calculations applied on a quarterly basis under such agreement, the Income Incentive Fee will be computed pursuant to the calculations hereunder on an annual basis and shall be subject to a single 8 percent hurdle rate such that no Income Incentive Fee will be paid unless the pre-Incentive Fee net operating income for the fiscal year in which it is calculated exceeds 8 percent of the Fund&#146;s aggregate NAV calculated as of the end of the fiscal year in which such fee is being calculated (the &#147;New Hurdle Amount&#148;) and the Income Incentive Fee shall be equal to the following: (i)&nbsp;50% of the amount by which such pre-Incentive Fee net operating income for the fiscal year exceeds the New Hurdle Amount but is less than 8.75% (the &#147;Catch-Up Hurdle&#148;); and (ii)&nbsp;20% of the amount by which such pre-Incentive Fee net operating income for the fiscal year equals or exceeds the Catch-Up Hurdle, subject to the qualifications/limitations below; (B)&nbsp;the Income Incentive Fee will be accrued only to the extent 20.0% of the cumulative net increase in net assets resulting from operations over the fiscal year for which such fees are being calculated and the 2 preceding fiscal years (but no earlier than the year ended October&nbsp;31, 2020) exceeds the cumulative Income Incentive Fees accrued and/or paid for such 2 fiscal years (but no earlier than the year ended October&nbsp;31, 2020). For the foregoing purposes, the &#147;cumulative net increases in net assets resulting from operations&#148; is the amount for the fiscal year of: the sum of pre-Incentive Fee net investment income (loss), realized gains and realized appreciation resulting from the &#147;Yield Portfolio&#148; (as defined by mutual agreement between the Company and the Adviser), less any realized losses and unrealized depreciation attributable to the Yield Portfolio, provided that such reductions (for losses/depreciation) shall be reduced by the amount of any carried-interest gains generated from the MVC PE Fund over the year for which such fees are being calculated and the 2 preceding fiscal years (but no earlier than the year ended October&nbsp;31, 2020), but only to the extent such carried-interest gains have not previously been applied to reduce losses/depreciation under this Clause (B); and (C)&nbsp;the amounts of any actual Income Incentive Fee payment reductions caused by application of clause (A)&nbsp;above (in lieu of applying the hurdle rates and catch up formula set forth in the Advisory Agreement) shall be credited against any unrealized depreciation or realized losses applied with respect to the application of Clause (B)&nbsp;above (on a one-time basis). Further, absent advance notice by the Adviser to the Board (at least 60 days&#146; prior to the fiscal year end), the Current Incentive Fee Modification shall continue automatically for each subsequent fiscal year.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">6.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b>Dividends and Distributions to Shareholders</b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a RIC, the Company is required to distribute to its shareholders, in a timely manner, at least 90% of its investment company taxable income and tax-exempt income each year.&#160; If the Company distributes, in a calendar year, at least 98% of its income and 98.2% of its capital gains of such calendar year (as well as any portion of the respective 2% balances not distributed in the previous </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Dividends and capital gain distributions, if any, are recorded on the ex-dividend date.&#160; Dividends and capital gain distributions are generally declared and paid quarterly according to the Company&#146;s policy established on July&nbsp;11, 2005. An additional distribution may be paid by the Company to avoid imposition of federal income tax on any remaining undistributed net investment income and capital gains. Distributions can be made payable by the Company either in the form of a cash distribution or a stock dividend.&#160; The amount and character of income and capital gain distributions are determined in accordance with income tax regulations which may differ from U.S. generally accepted accounting principles. These differences are due primarily to differing treatments of income and gain on various investment securities held by the Company, differing treatments of expenses paid by the Company, timing differences and differing characterizations of distributions made by the Company.&#160; Key examples of the primary differences in expenses paid are the accounting treatment of MVCFS (which is consolidated for GAAP purposes, but not income tax purposes) and the variation in treatment of incentive compensation expense.&#160; Permanent book and tax basis differences relating to shareholder distributions will result in reclassifications and may affect the allocation between net operating income, net realized gain (loss) and paid-in capital.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All of our shareholders who hold shares of common stock in their own name will automatically be enrolled in our dividend reinvestment plan (the &#147;Plan&#148;). All such shareholders will have any cash dividends and distributions automatically reinvested by the Plan Agent in additional shares of our common stock. Of course, any shareholder may elect to receive his or her dividends and distributions in cash. Currently, the Company has a policy of seeking to pay quarterly dividends to shareholders. For any of our shares that are held by banks, brokers or other entities that hold our shares as nominees for individual shareholders, the Plan Agent will administer the Plan on the basis of the number of shares certified by any nominee as being registered for shareholders that have not elected to receive dividends and distributions in cash. To receive your dividends and distributions in cash, shareholders must notify the Plan Agent, broker or other entity that holds the shares.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has procedures in place for the review, approval and monitoring of transactions involving the Company and certain persons related to the Company.&#160; For example, the Company has a Code of Ethics that generally prohibits, among others, any officer or director of the Company from engaging in any transaction where there is a conflict between such individual&#146;s personal interest and the interests of the Company.&#160; As a business development company, the 1940 Act also</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">imposes regulatory restrictions on the Company&#146;s ability to engage in certain related-party transactions.&#160; However, the Company is permitted to co-invest in certain portfolio companies with its affiliates to the extent consistent with applicable law or regulation and, if necessary, subject to specified conditions set forth in an exemptive order obtained from the SEC.&#160; On August&nbsp;28, 2017, the Company received an exemptive order from the SEC (the &#147;Order&#148;) that allows it to co-invest, subject to certain conditions, with certain affiliated private funds in first lien, second lien, mezzanine, structured debt and structured equity investments in small and middle market businesses and to undertake certain &#147;follow-on&#148; investments in companies in which the Fund has already co-invested pursuant to the Order. The Adviser has formed the TTGA C-I MMF LP (the &#147;Private Fund&#148;)&nbsp;&amp; TTGA C-1 LP funds, which were co-applicants for the granted exemptive relief.&#160; For the fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2018 and October&nbsp;31, 2019, there were 6 and 1 investments, respectively, made pursuant to the Order.&#160; See Item 7 &#151; Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, &#147;Portfolio Investments&#148; for more information.&#160; As a matter of policy, our Board has required that any related-party transaction (as defined in Item 404 of Regulation S-K) must be subject to the advance consideration and approval of the Independent Directors, in accordance with applicable procedures set forth in Section&nbsp;57(f)&nbsp;of the 1940 Act.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial instruments that subjected the Company to concentrations of market risk consisted principally of equity investments, subordinated notes, debt instruments and escrow receivables (other than cash equivalents), which collectively represented approximately 94.3% and 93.8% of the Company&#146;s total assets at October&nbsp;31, 2019 and October&nbsp;31, 2018, respectively. As discussed in Note 9, these investments consist of securities in companies with no readily determinable market values and as such are valued in accordance with the Company&#146;s fair value policies and procedures. The Company&#146;s investment strategy represents a high degree of business and financial risk due to the fact</font>  </font>that the Company&#146;s portfolio investments (other than cash equivalents) are generally illiquid, in small and middle market companies, and include foreign investments (which subject the Company to additional risks such as currency, geographic, demographic and operational risks), entities with little operating history or entities that possess operations in new or developing industries. These investments, should they become publicly traded, would generally be (i)&nbsp;subject to restrictions on resale, if they were acquired from the issuer in private placement transactions; and (ii)&nbsp;susceptible to market risk.&#160; Additionally, we are classified as a non-diversified investment</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is classified as a non-diversified investment company within the meaning of the 1940 Act, and therefore we may invest a significant portion of our assets in a relatively small number of portfolio companies in a limited number of industries.&#160; Beyond the asset diversification requirements associated with our qualification as a RIC, we do not have fixed guidelines for diversification, and while we are not targeting any specific industries, relatively few industries may continue to be significantly represented among our investments.&#160; To the extent that we have large positions in the securities of a small number of portfolio companies, we are subject to an increased risk of significant loss should the performance or financial condition of these portfolio companies or their respective industries deteriorate.&#160; We may also be more susceptible to any single economic or regulatory occurrence as a result of holding large positions in a small number of portfolio companies.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">9.</font></b>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <b>Portfolio Investments</b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pursuant to the requirements of the 1940 Act and ASC 820, we value our portfolio securities at their current market values or, if market quotations are not readily available, at their estimates of fair values. Because our portfolio company investments generally do not have readily ascertainable market values, we record these investments at fair value in accordance with Valuation Procedures adopted by our Board of Directors.&#160; As permitted by the SEC, the Board of Directors has delegated the responsibility of making fair value determinations to the Valuation Committee, subject to the Board of Directors&#146; supervision and pursuant to our Valuation Procedures.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The levels of fair value inputs used to measure our investments are characterized in accordance with the fair value hierarchy established by ASC 820. Where inputs for an asset or liability fall in more than one level in the fair value hierarchy, the investment is classified in its entirety based on the lowest level input that is significant to that investment&#146;s fair value measurement. We use judgment and consider factors specific to the investment in determining the significance of an input to a fair value measurement. The three levels of the fair value hierarchy and investments that fall into each of the levels are described below:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><i style="font-weight:bold;">Level 1:</i></b> Level 1 inputs are unadjusted quoted prices in active markets that are accessible at the measurement date for identical, unrestricted assets or liabilities. We use Level 1 inputs for investments in publicly traded unrestricted securities for which we do not have a controlling interest. Such investments are valued at the closing price on the measurement date.&#160; We valued one of our investments using Level 1 inputs as of October&nbsp;31, 2019.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
