<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><i style="font-weight:bold;">Level 2:</i></b> Level 2 inputs are inputs other than quoted prices included within Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly or other inputs that are observable or can be corroborated by observable market data. Additionally, the Company&#146;s interests in Investment Vehicles that can be withdrawn by the Company at the net asset value reported by such Investment Vehicle as of the measurement date or within six months of the measurement date are generally categorized as Level 2 investments.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b><i style="font-weight:bold;">Level 3:</i></b> Level 3 inputs are unobservable and cannot be corroborated by observable market data. Additionally, included in Level 3 are the Company&#146;s interests in Investment Vehicles from which the Company cannot withdraw at the net asset value reported by such Investment Vehicles as of the measurement date, or within six months of the measurement date.&#160; We use Level 3 inputs for measuring the fair value of substantially all of our investments. See Note 3 &#147;Significant Accounting Policies&#148; for the investment valuation policies used to determine the fair value of these investments.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As noted above, the interests in Investment Vehicles are included in Level 2 or 3 of the fair value hierarchy.&#160; In determining the appropriate level, the Company considers the length of time until the investment is redeemable, including notice and lock-up periods and any other restriction on the disposition of the investment.&#160; The Company also considers the nature of the portfolios of the underlying Investment Vehicles and such vehicles&#146; ability to liquidate their investment.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A review of fair value hierarchy classifications is conducted on a quarterly basis.&#160; Changes in the observability of valuation inputs may result in a reclassification for certain financial assets or liabilities.&#160; Reclassifications impacting Level 3 of the fair value hierarchy are reported as transfers in/out of the Level 3 category as of the beginning of the period in which the reclassifications occur.&#160; During the fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2019 and October&nbsp;31, 2018, there were no transfers in and out of Level 1 or 2.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">changes in unobservable inputs and the interrelationships between those unobservable inputs, if any.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Following are descriptions of the sensitivity of the Level 3 recurring fair value measurements to changes in the significant unobservable inputs presented in the above table.&#160; For securities utilizing the income approach valuation technique, a significant increase (decrease) in the discount rate, risk premium or discount for lack of marketability would result in a significantly lower (higher) fair value measurement. The discount for lack of marketability used to determine fair value may include other factors such as liquidity or credit risk. Generally, a change in the discount rate is accompanied by a directionally similar change in the risk premium and discount for lack of marketability.&#160; For securities utilizing the market approach valuation technique, a significant increase (decrease) in the EBITDA, revenue multiple or other key unobservable inputs listed in the above table would result in a significantly higher (lower) fair value measurement. A significant increase (decrease) in the discount for lack of marketability would result in a significantly lower (higher) fair value measurement. The discount for lack of marketability used to determine fair value may include other factors such as liquidity or credit risk.&#160; For securities utilizing an adjusted net asset approach valuation technique, a significant increase (decrease) in the price to book value ratio, discount rate or other key unobservable inputs listed in the above table would result in a significantly higher (lower) fair value measurement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36.4pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the Fiscal Year Ended October&nbsp;31, 2019</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2019, the Company made six new investments, committing capital that totaled approximately $32.4 million.&#160; Pursuant to an exemptive order received by the Company from the SEC (the &#147;Order&#148;), that allows the Company to co-invest, subject to certain conditions, with certain affiliated private funds as described in the Order, each of the Company and the Private Fund co-invested in GTM ($1.9 million investment for the Company).&#160; The Company also invested in Powers ($6.5 million),&nbsp;IPCC ($8.0 million), Jedson ($6.0 million), SMA ($7.0 million) and Global Prairie ($3.0 million).</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2019, the Company made follow-on investments in six portfolio companies that totaled approximately $12.5 million.&#160; On December&nbsp;21, 2018, the Company loaned an additional $2.0 million to Custom Alloy in the form of a second lien loan with an interest rate of 11% and a maturity date of December&nbsp;23, 2019.&#160; During the fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2019, the Company loaned approximately $1.4 million to RuMe and received a new warrant.&#160; On June&nbsp;7, 2019, the Company invested approximately $3.9 million in GTM increasing the second lien loan by $3.5 million and investing approximately $420,000 for additional common shares.&#160; During the fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2019, Custom Alloy borrowed approximately $2.1 million on its revolving credit facility with a 15% interest rate and a maturity date of April&nbsp;30, 2020.&#160; On July&nbsp;15, 2019, the Company loaned an additional $1.0 million to HTI increasing its second lien loan to approximately $11.4 million as of October&nbsp;31, 2019.&#160; On September&nbsp;10, 2019, the Company invested $1.0 million in MVC Automotive in the form of additional common equity.&#160; On September&nbsp;26, 2019, the Company loaned approximately $552,000 to Security Holdings, increasing the senior subordinated loan to approximately $6.0 million as of October&nbsp;31, 2019.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;9, 2018, Custom Alloy repaid its first lien loan in full, including all accrued interest.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">securities.&#160; As of October&nbsp;31, 2019, the Company was in compliance with all covenants related to Credit Facility II.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;9, 2015, the Company entered into a three-year,&nbsp;$50 million revolving borrowing base credit facility (&#147;Credit Facility III&#148;) with&nbsp;Santander Bank&nbsp;N.A. as a lender and lead agent and&nbsp;Wintrust Bank&nbsp;as a lender and syndication agent. &nbsp;Credit Facility III was to expire on December&nbsp;9, 2018.&#160; Credit Facility III can, under certain conditions, be increased up to&nbsp;$85 million.&#160; The new facility bears an interest rate of LIBOR plus 3.75% or the prime rate plus 1% (at the Company&#146;s option), and includes a 1% closing fee of the commitment amount and a 0.75% unused fee.&#160; The compensating balance for the revolving credit facility is $5.0 million, which is reflected as restricted cash or cash equivalents on the Company&#146;s Consolidated Balance Sheets.&nbsp; On February&nbsp;26, 2018, in connection with the U.S. Gas Sale, Credit Facility III was amended, effective as of July&nbsp;5, 2017, to exclude from pledged collateral the U.S. Gas second lien loan.&#160; On May&nbsp;7, 2018, the terms of Credit Facility III were amended to, among other things: (i)&nbsp;increase the limit for unsecured indebtedness and certain unsecured guaranty obligations of portfolio companies of the Company to $10,000,000 and (ii)&nbsp;increase the limit on permitted investments of the Company with respect to certain debt, equity and follow-on investments to $28,500,000.&#160; All other material terms of Credit Facility III remained unchanged.&#160; As of October&nbsp;31, 2018, there was no outstanding balance on Credit Facility III and the Company was in compliance with all covenants related to Credit Facility III.&#160; On December&nbsp;7, 2018, Credit Facility III was renewed until March&nbsp;9, 2019.&#160; On January&nbsp;29, 2019, Credit Facility III was terminated.&#160;&#160;&#160; As of October&nbsp;31, 2019, Credit Facility III was no longer a commitment of the Company.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;15, 2017, the Company completed a public offering of $100,000,000 aggregate principal amount of its 6.25% senior notes due November&nbsp;30, 2022 (&#147;Senior Notes II&#148;). In addition, on November&nbsp;20, 2017, the underwriters exercised an over-allotment option to purchase an additional $15 million in aggregate principal amount of Senior Notes II (together with the offering on November&nbsp;15, the &#147;Offering&#148;).&#160; The Senior Notes II have an interest rate of 6.25% per year payable quarterly on January&nbsp;15, April&nbsp;15, July&nbsp;15, and October&nbsp;15 of each year.&#160; After deducting underwriting fees and discounts and expenses, the Offering resulted in net proceeds to the Company of approximately $111.4 million.&#160; The Offering expenses incurred are amortized over the term of the Senior Notes II.&#160; Proceeds from the offering were used to repay the Senior Notes in full, including all accrued interest.&#160; As of October&nbsp;31, 2019, the Senior Notes II had a total outstanding amount of $115.0 million, net of deferred financing fees the balance was approximately $112.7 million, with a market value of approximately $116.7 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;29, 2019, the Company entered into a three year, $35 million revolving credit facility (&#147;Credit Facility IV&#148;) with People&#146;s United Bank, National Association as lender and lead agent. Credit Facility IV can, under certain conditions, be increased up to $85 million. Credit Facility IV will expire on January&nbsp;29, 2022, at which time all outstanding amounts under Credit Facility IV will be due and payable.&#160; Borrowings under the Credit Facility bear interest at a rate of LIBOR plus 2.85%, or the prime rate plus 0.5% at the Company&#146;s discretion. In addition, the Company was subject to (i)&nbsp;a closing fee of 1% of the commitment amount paid at closing, (ii)&nbsp;a one-time structuring fee in the amount of $100,000 paid at closing, (iii)&nbsp;an unused line fee, which is payable monthly, of 0.75% if the Company draws less than $25 million on Credit Facility IV or 0.60% if the Company draws more than $25 million on Credit Facility IV, and (iv)&nbsp;an annual administrative agent fee in the amount of $100,000 in 2019 and $200,000 in each year thereafter. The compensating balance for the revolving credit facility is $5.0 million, which is reflected as </font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;">147<a name="PB_147_133421_5926"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">restricted cash equivalents on the Company&#146;s Consolidated Balance Sheets.&nbsp; On June&nbsp;19, 2019, in order to increase the size of the Credit Facility IV, the credit facility was amended to add Bank Leumi USA as an additional lender. The amendment increased the size of Credit Facility IV by $15.0 million to $50.0 million. All other material terms of the Credit Facility remain unchanged. In addition, the Company was subject to a closing fee of 1% of the additional commitment amount of $15.0 million to be paid at closing.&#160; As of October&nbsp;31, 2019, there was $15.1 million outstanding on Credit Facility IV and the Company was in compliance with the maximum balance sheet leverage covenant related to Credit Facility IV.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company enters into contracts with portfolio companies and other parties that contain a variety of indemnifications. The Company&#146;s maximum exposure under these arrangements is unknown. However, the Company has not experienced claims or losses pursuant to these contracts and believes the risk of loss related to indemnifications to be remote.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">11.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b>Certain Issuances of Equity Securities by the Issuer and Share Repurchase Program</b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On April&nbsp;3, 2013, the Company&#146;s Board of Directors authorized an expanded share repurchase program to opportunistically buy back shares in the market in an effort to narrow the market discount of its shares.&#160; The previously authorized $5 million limit has been eliminated.&#160; Under the repurchase program, shares may be repurchased from time to time at prevailing market prices. The repurchase program does not obligate the Company to acquire any specific number of shares and may be discontinued at any time.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On September&nbsp;18, 2018, the Company&#146;s Board of Directors approved the Company&#146;s implementation of a&nbsp;$10 million&nbsp;stock repurchase program.&nbsp; The program, which was to be completed by the end of the 2018 calendar year, was to consist of an issuer tender offer and/or open market repurchases.&nbsp; In addition, the Company&#146;s Board of Directors directed the Company to pursue an additional&nbsp;$5 million&nbsp;in stock repurchases in the open market in 2019, using a portion of the proceeds of equity monetizations and subject to MVC&#146;s common stock continuing to trade at a significant discount to NAV.&nbsp; Open market repurchases would be made pursuant to the Company&#146;s unlimited stock repurchase program adopted in 2013.&#160; On October&nbsp;11, 2018, pursuant to the repurchase program, the Company entered into the Rule&nbsp;10b5-1 Plan that qualifies for the safe harbors provided by Rules&nbsp;10b5-1 and 10b-18 under the Exchange Act. See the Company&#146;s current report on Form&nbsp;8-K, filed on October&nbsp;12, 2018, for further details regarding the 10b5-1 Plan.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;28, 2018, the Company announced its determination to extend the repurchase program beyond December&nbsp;31, 2018 until the full $10 million of shares are repurchased pursuant to the repurchase program.&#160; During the fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2019, the Company completed the repurchase program.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table represents open-market purchases made under our stock repurchase program for the fiscal years ended October&nbsp;31, 2013 through October&nbsp;31, 2019.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">TENDER OFFERS</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;21, 2017, the Company commenced a modified &#147;Dutch Auction&#148; tender offer (the &#147;Tender Offer&#148;) to purchase up to $15 million of its common stock at a price per share not less than $10.00 and not greater than $11.00 in $0.20 increments. The Company&#146;s Tender Offer expired at 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on August&nbsp;18, 2017. A total of 3,634,597 shares of the Company&#146;s common stock were properly tendered and not properly withdrawn at or below a purchase price of $10.40 per share. In accordance with the terms and conditions of the Tender Offer, the Company accepted for payment, on a pro rata basis, at a purchase price of $10.40,&nbsp;1,442,307 shares properly tendered at or below the purchase price and not properly withdrawn before the expiration date, at an aggregate cost of approximately $15.0 million, excluding fees and expenses relating to the Tender Offer.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;22, 2017, the Company commenced a modified &#147;Dutch Auction&#148; tender offer (the &#147;TO&#148;) to purchase up to $25 million of its common stock at a price per share not less than $10.40 and not greater than $11.00 in $0.10 increments.&#160; The TO expired at 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on December&nbsp;21, 2017.&#160; In accordance with the terms and conditions of the TO, the Company accepted for payment, at a purchase price of $10.90,&nbsp;2,293,577 shares properly tendered at or below the purchase price, at an aggregate cost of approximately $25.0 million, excluding fees and expenses relating to the TO.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">12.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b>Tax Matters</b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Return of Capital Statement of Position (ROCSOP) Adjustment:</font></u></i> During the year ended October&nbsp;31, 2019, the Company recorded a reclassification for permanent book to tax differences. These differences were primarily due to the sale of distressed securities, reclassifications from partnerships and character of PIK payments in preferred stock and settlement income received. These differences resulted in a net increase in accumulated income of $7,123,905, a decrease in </p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company designated 31.27% of dividends declared and paid during the year ending October&nbsp;31, 2019 from net investment income as qualified dividend income under the Jobs Growth and Tax Relief Reconciliation Act of 2003.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Corporate Dividends Received Deduction Percentage</font></u></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Corporate shareholders may be eligible for the dividends received deduction for certain ordinary income distributions paid by the Company. The Company designated 31.27% of dividends declared and paid during the year ending October&nbsp;31, 2019 from net investment income as qualifying for the dividends received deduction. The deduction is a pass through of dividends paid by domestic corporations (i.e. only equities) subject to taxation.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Qualified Interest Related Dividends Percentage</font></u></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company designated 76.69% of dividends declared and paid during the year ending October&nbsp;31, 2019 from net investment income as interest related dividends under Internal Revenue Code Section&nbsp;871(k)(1)(c).</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Short-Term Capital Gain Dividends Percentage</font></u></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company designated 0% of dividends declared and paid during the year ending October&nbsp;31, 2019 from ordinary income as short-term capital gain dividends under Internal Revenue Code Section&nbsp;871(k)(2)(c).</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">13.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b>Income Taxes</b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:17.85pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s wholly-owned subsidiary MVCFS is subject to federal and state income tax. For the fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2019, the Company recorded a tax provision of $1,929. For the fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2018, the Company recorded a tax provision of $1,922. For the fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2017, the Company recorded a tax provision of $1,920. The provision for income taxes was comprised of the following:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</font></b><a name="ReportofIndependentRegisteredPub_082529"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Board of Directors and Shareholders</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">MVC Capital,&nbsp;Inc.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Opinion on the financial statements</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of MVC Capital,&nbsp;Inc. (a Delaware corporation) and subsidiaries (the &#147;Company&#148;), including the consolidated schedule of investments, as of October&nbsp;31, 2019 and 2018, the related consolidated statements of operations, cash flows and changes in net assets for each of the three years in the period ended October&nbsp;31, 2019, and the related notes and selected per share data and ratios and financial statement schedule included under Item 15(a)(2)&nbsp; (collectively referred to as the &#147;financial statements&#148;). In our opinion, the financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of October&nbsp;31, 2019 and 2018, and the results of its operations, its cash flows and changes in net assets for each of the three years in the period ended October&nbsp;31, 2019, and its selected per share data and ratios for each of the five years in the period ended October&nbsp;31, 2019, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (&#147;PCAOB&#148;), the Company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting as of October&nbsp;31, 2019, based on criteria established in the 2013 <i>Internal Control&#151;Integrated Framework</i> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (&#147;COSO&#148;), and our report dated January&nbsp;14, 2020 expressed an unqualified opinion.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Basis for opinion</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">These financial statements are the responsibility of the Company&#146;s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company&#146;s financial statements based on our audits. We are a public accounting firm registered with the PCAOB and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules&nbsp;and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. Our audits included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. Our procedures included verification by confirmation of securities as of October&nbsp;31, 2019 and 2018, by correspondence with the portfolio companies and custodians. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the financial statements. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-1.0in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 9.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b>CHANGES IN AND DISAGREEMENTS WITH ACCOUNTANTS ON ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE</b><a name="Item9_CHANGESINANDDISAGREEMENTSW_014404"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">None.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-1.0in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM 9A.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b>CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES</b><a name="ITEM9A_CONTROLSANDPROCEDURES_014408"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management has conducted an evaluation, under the supervision of, and with the participation of, the individual who performs the functions of a Principal Executive Officer (the &#147;CEO&#148;) and the individual who performs the functions of a Principal Financial Officer (the &#147;CFO&#148;), of the effectiveness of the design and operation of the Company&#146;s disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rule&nbsp;13a-15(e)&nbsp;under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the &#147;Exchange Act&#148;)) as of October&nbsp;31, 2019. Based upon that evaluation, management has concluded that the Company&#146;s disclosure controls and procedures are effective as of October&nbsp;31, 2019.&nbsp; Disclosure controls and procedures are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in company reports filed or submitted under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the Securities and Exchange Commission&#146;s rules&nbsp;and forms. Disclosure controls and procedures include, without limitation, controls and procedures designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in company reports filed under the Exchange Act is accumulated and communicated to management, including the Company&#146;s CEO and CFO as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Management&#146;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">General.</font></i> The Company&#146;s management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting as defined in Rule&nbsp;13a-15(f)&nbsp;of the Exchange Act. The Company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting is designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Scope of Management&#146;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting.</font></i> The Company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that:</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>pertain to the maintenance of records that in reasonable detail accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the Company;</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that the Company&#146;s receipts and expenditures are being made only in accordance with authorizations of the Company&#146;s management and directors; and</p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use or disposition of the Company&#146;s assets that could have a material effect on the Company&#146;s financial statements.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management, including the Company&#146;s CEO and CFO, assessed the effectiveness of the Company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting as of October&nbsp;31, 2019. In making this assessment, management used the criteria established in the 2013 Internal Control-Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO). Based on management&#146;s assessment, management concluded that the Company maintained effective internal control over financial reporting as of October&nbsp;31, 2019.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:20.55pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management does not expect that the Company&#146;s disclosure controls and procedures or the Company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting will prevent or detect all error and all fraud. A control system, regardless of how well conceived and operated, can provide only reasonable, not absolute, assurance that the objectives of the control system will be met. Because of the inherent limitations in all control systems, no evaluation of controls can provide absolute assurance that all control issues and instances of fraud, if any, have been detected. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Attestation Report of the Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s financial statements have been audited by Grant Thornton LLP (&#147;Grant Thornton&#148;), an independent registered public accounting firm.&nbsp; Grant Thornton&#146;s attestation report on the Company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting is included herein.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There has been no change in the Company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting that occurred during the fiscal quarter ended October&nbsp;31, 2019, that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, the Company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Board of Directors and Shareholders</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">MVC Capital,&nbsp;Inc.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Opinion on internal control over financial reporting</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have audited the internal control over financial reporting of MVC Capital,&nbsp;Inc. (a Delaware corporation) and subsidiaries (the &#147;Company&#148;) as of October&nbsp;31, 2019, based on criteria established in the 2013 <i>Internal Control&#151;Integrated Framework</i> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (&#147;COSO&#148;). In our opinion, the Company maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of October&nbsp;31, 2019, based on criteria established in the 2013 <i>Internal Control&#151;Integrated Framework</i> issued by COSO.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (&#147;PCAOB&#148;), the consolidated financial statements of the Company as of and for the year ended October&nbsp;31, 2019, and our report dated January&nbsp;14, 2020 expressed an unqualified opinion on those financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Basis for opinion</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, included in the accompanying Management&#146;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting based on our audit. We are a public accounting firm registered with the PCAOB and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules&nbsp;and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects. Our audit included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk, and performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Definition and limitations of internal control over financial reporting</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1)&nbsp;pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company&#146;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In determining to propose each of the nominees for election by stockholders as Directors, the Nominating Committee and the Board considered a variety of factors, including their professional background and experience and, in the case of the nominees who are currently serving as directors, their ongoing contributions to the Board. Mr.&nbsp;Douglas Kass was elected as a Director at the 2019 Annual Meeting. He was nominated on the recommendation of a stockholder. In particular, the Nominating Committee and the Board considered Mr.&nbsp;Kass&#146;s background and experience in financing and investments. The Board noted the nominees&#146; collective knowledge and experience in financial services, legal and financial analysis, corporate finance, asset management, portfolio management and accounting, all of which strengthen the Board&#146;s collective qualifications. The Nominating Committee members considered that Messrs.&nbsp;Tokarz and Holtsberg are not Independent Directors but recognized that they represent the Adviser, and, as such, help foster the Board&#146;s direct access to information regarding the Adviser, which is the Fund&#146;s most significant service provider.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Section&nbsp;16(a)&nbsp;Beneficial Ownership Reporting Compliance.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Section&nbsp;16(a)&nbsp;of the 1934 Act, and Section&nbsp;30(h)&nbsp;of the 1940 Act, taken together, require that the Directors, officers of the Company and beneficial owners of more than 10% of the equity securities of the Company (collectively, &#147;Reporting Persons&#148;) file with the SEC reports of their beneficial ownership and changes in their beneficial ownership of the Company&#146;s securities. Based solely on its review of the copies of such reports, the Company believes that each of the Reporting Persons who was a Reporting Person during the fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2019 has complied with applicable filing requirements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36.4pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Code of Ethics.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36.4pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Board has also adopted a Code of Ethics, which applies to, among others, all of the Company&#146;s officers and directors, as well as a Code of Ethics for Principal Executive and Senior Financial Executives that applies to and has been signed by the Principal Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer of the Company. You may read and copy the Codes of Ethics at the SEC&#146;s Public Reference Room located at 100&nbsp;F&nbsp;Street, NE, Washington, DC 20549. You may obtain information on the operation of the Public Reference Room by calling the SEC at 1-800-SEC-0330. In addition, the Codes of Ethics are available on the EDGAR Database on the SEC&#146;s website at <i>http://www.sec.gov. </i>These materials can also be found on the Company&#146;s website at www.mvccapital.com. Waivers, if any, of the Company&#146;s Code of Ethics or Code of Ethics for Principal Executive and Senior Financial Executives will be promptly disclosed on the Company&#146;s website.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36.4pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Audit Committee.</font></b></p>

The members of the Audit Committee are Emilio Dominianni, Gerald Hellerman and William Taylor.&nbsp; Each of the current members of the Audit Committee, is considered an independent director.&nbsp; Each member of the Audit Committee meets the applicable independence and experience requirements, and the Board has determined that Mr.&nbsp;Hellerman is an &#147;audit committee financial expert,&#148; as defined under Item 407(d)(5)&nbsp;of </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:19.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s officers do not receive any direct compensation from the Company. The Company does not currently have any employees and does not expect to have any employees. Services necessary for its business are provided by individuals who are employees of the Adviser, and the Company&#146;s administrator, U.S. Bancorp Fund Services, LLC (the &#147;Administrator&#148;), pursuant to the terms of the Company&#146;s amended and restated investment advisory and management agreement (the &#147;Advisory Agreement&#148;) and administration agreement. Each of the Company&#146;s executive officers is an employee of the Adviser. The Company&#146;s day-to-day investment operations are managed by the Adviser.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:19.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table sets forth compensation paid by the Company in all capacities during the fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2019 to all of our Directors. Our Directors have been divided into two groups&#151;Interested Directors and Independent Directors. The Interested Directors are &#147;interested persons,&#148; as defined in the 1940 Act, of the Company. No compensation is paid to the Interested Directors. (The Company is not part of any Fund Complex.) No information has been provided with respect to executive officers of the Company because the Company&#146;s executive officers do not receive any direct compensation from the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36.4pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Compensation Committee.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Compensation Committee, the principal purpose of which is to oversee the compensation of the Independent Directors, is currently comprised of Messrs.&nbsp;Hellerman and Knapp. Mr.&nbsp;Hellerman is the Chairman of the Compensation Committee. The Compensation Committee was established in March&nbsp;2003. The Compensation Committee annually reviews the overall compensation principles of the Company governing the compensation and benefits of the Directors and officers, including developing and recommending, for the Board&#146;s adoption, compensation for members of the Board.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has procedures in place for the review, approval and monitoring of transactions involving the Company and certain persons related to the Company. For example, the Company has a Code of Ethics that generally prohibits, among others, any officer or director of the Company from engaging in any transaction where there is a conflict between such individual&#146;s personal interest and the interests of the Company. As a business development company, the 1940 </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Act also imposes regulatory restrictions on the Company&#146;s ability to engage in certain related-party transactions. However, the Company is permitted to co-invest in certain portfolio companies with its affiliates to the extent consistent with applicable law or regulation and, if necessary, subject to specified conditions set forth in an exemptive order obtained from the SEC. On August&nbsp;28, 2017, the Company received an exemptive order from the SEC (the &#147;Order&#148;) that allows it to co-invest, subject to certain conditions, with certain affiliated private funds in first lien, second lien, mezzanine, structured debt and structured equity investments in small and middle market businesses and to undertake certain &#147;follow-on&#148; investments in companies in which the Company has already co-invested pursuant to the Order. TTG Advisers has formed the TTGA C-I MMF LP (the &#147;Insurance Fund&#148;)&nbsp;&amp; TTGA C-1 LP funds, which were co-applicants for the granted exemptive relief. For the fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2019, there was one (1)&nbsp;investment made pursuant to the Order. As a matter of policy, our Board has required that any related-party transaction (as defined in Item 404 of Regulation S-K) must be subject to the advance consideration and approval of the Independent Directors, in accordance with applicable procedures set forth in Section&nbsp;57(f)&nbsp;of the 1940 Act.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The principal equity owner of TTG Advisers is Mr.&nbsp;Tokarz, our Chairman. Our senior officers and Mr.&nbsp;Holtsberg, a Director of the Company, have other financial interests in TTG Advisers (i.e., based on TTG Advisers&#146; performance). In addition, our officers and the officers and employees of TTG Advisers may serve as officers, directors or principals of entities that operate in the same or related line of business as we do or of investment funds managed by TTG Advisers or our affiliates. However, TTG Advisers intends to allocate investment opportunities in a fair and equitable manner. Our Board of Directors has approved a specific policy in this regard that is set forth in the present Form&nbsp;10-K for the fiscal year ended October&nbsp;31, 2019.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Further, Mr.&nbsp;Tokarz is a co-founder of PPC Enterprises LLC (&#147;PPC&#148;), a registered investment adviser that provides advisory services to Series&nbsp;A of Public Pension Capital, LLC (the &#147;PPC Fund&#148;). As a result of this relationship and pursuant to a shared services arrangement with PPC, certain of PPC&#146;s principals and other PPC investment professionals may make themselves available, from time to time, to consult with the Adviser on investment matters relating to MVC or the PE Fund. In this connection, certain employees of PPC are &#147;associated persons&#148; of TTG Advisers when providing certain services on behalf of the Adviser and, in this capacity, are subject to its oversight and supervision. Likewise, the Adviser makes available to PPC certain investment professionals that are employed by the Adviser to provide services for PPC and the PPC Fund.</font></p>
